Weight gain or loss is a math equation: calories in vs. calories used. There is no other truth to it than that. To be clear:

  • You cannot gain weight without taking in more calories than your body uses.
  • You cannot lose weight without burning more calories than you take in.

Drugs or depression may incline you to eat more or to be less discerning in what you eat, but neither can make calories magically appear or disappear around your waistline.

While there are medications that can increase/decrease your metabolism, at the very most a 'slow metabolism' will decrease your resting calories burned by ~300.

You might have to eat less (or exercise more) than you would while not taking the medication in order to keep yourself from gaining weight, but the mechanics of weightloss are eternally bound to 'did you eat more calories than you burned today?'

I drive at 15 mph. I turn the steering wheel a half-circle right. I let go of the steering wheel and the car-wheels automatically straighten themselves (point forwards) instead of continuing to point right. Why is this?
Why do car-wheels automatically straighten when you let go of the steering wheel?

The tire is not a point so while the car is turning both sides of the tire are sliding. Only the center is actually turning in sync with the road. Since the two sides are sliding over the pavement in opposite directions it torques the wheel pulling it straight.
So if the wheels were to be turned further than 90 degrees in a direction, they would not automatically turn facing forward (but rather try to turn backwards)?

Yes that's why most vehicles don't have that much turning ability. The vehicle has natural stability to go straight, that decreases as you turn. At 90° it becomes naturally unstable and trends to spin.
In reality the reason is because the wheels trail slightly behind the steering axis, like a grocery cart caster wheel.
